item: bind the freshness stamp to a source hash: extend tools/freshness_gate.py (t11b's tool, t11b's next_steal) to accept an optional source-hash binding (receipt format source-fetched: DATE sha256:HASH); when the gated receipt cites a file that exists, recompute its hash and fail if it differs, so re-stamping old claims fails the gate; keep fail-closed and the --days override untouched; tests for hash-match passes / hash-mismatch fails / no-hash behaves as before; run pytest + violation_ratchet check --changed and cite raw output
note: source-hash binding landed on tools/freshness_gate.py. Stamp lines may now carry sha256:<64 hex> after the date; --source PATH makes the binding load-bearing. Behavior: binding + cited file exists -> gate recomputes sha256 over file bytes, match exits 0 with 'verified' in the reason, mismatch exits 2 naming both hex digests; cited file missing exits 2; --source given but receipt binds nothing exits 2; binding stamped with no --source keeps date-only rules and reports 'stamped but unverified'; newest stamp dropping a binding an older stamp carried exits 2 (re-stamp smell) even without --source, so appending a bare fresh stamp cannot launder a bound claim; a stamp line that says sha256 with a malformed binding (63/65 chars, non-hex) voids the whole stamp (exit 2, same rule as an unparseable date), never a truncated-hash guess. Fail-closed throughout; --days and all t11b date rules untouched. Gate result dict adds keys hash and hash_ok (True/False/None) beside the t11b contract. Contract proven live seven ways (match 0, mismatch 2, missing 2, source-without-binding 2, re-stamp-drop 2, unverified 0, --days 1 -> 2 and --days 30 -> 2 via mismatch). Negatives recorded: (1) my first rewrite dropped the ? that made the hash regex group optional, 14/31 tests failed including every plain t11b stamp, caught by pytest, fixed before banking, raw failure output kept in t37.check.txt section D; (2) first live CLI demo died because mktemp -d hands Git Bash a /tmp path Windows python does not map, redone with cygpath -m, failed run preserved in section E; (3) full-scope ratchet not run, --changed scope only, per t11b precedent (full-scope NEW hits in unowned files were recorded there and not repaired here).
